items.stem: A route uses rides of 8, 12 and 23 minutes. Each ride costs 13 pesos. What are the total minutes and fare?

options.feedback: The fare is charged for each ride. Three rides cost 3 times 13 pesos.
8 + 12 + 23 is 43 minutes. Three rides at 13 pesos each cost 39 pesos.
The two totals are swapped. Minutes add up the ride times, and the fare counts rides.

items.stem: A flood closes the line from Marikina to Ortigas. An app that stored the old best route keeps sending riders into the flood. What would have avoided this?

options.text: Storing a second best route in advance for each trip.
options.feedback: A stored route fails the same way when one of its own lines closes.

options.text: Telling riders to check the news before they travel.
options.feedback: That hands the work to riders, and the app still gives wrong answers.

options.text: Searching the current map each time and skipping closed lines.
options.feedback: A method that works on whatever map is open finds a new route when a line closes.

items.stem: A commuter picks the route with the fewest rides. It takes 43 minutes. Another route takes 38 minutes and has one more ride. Which statement fits?

options.text: Each route wins on one measure, so the commuter chooses which counts more.
options.feedback: Shortest time and fewest rides give different winners, and only the commuter knows the priority.

options.text: The 38 minute route is better, because time always matters most.
options.feedback: It saves 5 minutes and adds a ride and a 13 peso fare. Some commuters would not accept that.

options.text: The fewest-rides route is a mistake and should be dropped.
options.feedback: It is the best route for the measure it uses, which is the number of rides.

items.stem: A startup builds a delivery app. Which question is a routing problem?

options.text: Which color should the delivery button be?
options.feedback: Color is a design choice. It has nothing to do with paths.

options.text: Which order of stops delivers six parcels fastest?
options.feedback: It asks for the best path through places joined by roads.

options.text: How many riders should the startup hire?
options.feedback: That is a staffing question. A route does not answer it.
